messages.subject: Clarification regarding LkjCholeksy
parts:
Hi

Page 414 of the manual documents the pdf of the LkjCholesky(L|eta). I am wondering whether the exponent of L_{kk} in the product be (K-k+2\eta-1), instead of (K-k+2\eta-2) as reported. 

Thanks

Asim

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Clarification regarding LkjCholeksy
parts:
On Saturday, August 29, 2015 at 5:35:08 PM UTC-4, Asim Ansari wrote:
Page 414 of the manual documents the pdf of the LkjCholesky(L|eta). I am wondering whether the exponent of L_{kk} in the product be (K-k+2\eta-1), instead of (K-k+2\eta-2) as reported.

I think the manual is right. You've got a density proportional to |J| |LL'|^(eta - 1), which we can simplify using the fact that |LL'| = |L|^2 and |L| is the product of the diagonal elements of L. So the density is proportional to |J| |L|^(2eta - 2) and then the |J| contributes the K - k piece in the exponent.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Clarification regarding LkjCholeksy
parts:
Yes, The density portion is fine, but isn't the Jacobian determinant supposed to 2^K* \prod_{k=1}^{K} L_{kk}^(K+1-k) for a Cholesky transformation? 

The document  (http://web.mit.edu/18.325/www/handouts/handout2.pdf), page 13 refers to the above result.

On Saturday, August 29, 2015 at 7:07:58 PM UTC-4, Asim Ansari wrote:

Yes, The density portion is fine, but isn't the Jacobian determinant supposed to 2^K* \prod_{k=1}^{K} L_{kk}^(K+1-k) for a Cholesky transformation? 

The document  (http://web.mit.edu/18.325/www/handouts/handout2.pdf), page 13 refers to the above result.

Edelman's notes pertain to the Cholesky factorization of a general positive definite covariance matrix. In this case LL' is a correlation matrix so L[1,1] = 1 rather than being a free parameter as in the general case. If I am remembering correctly, that is the reason why the exponent looks off-by-one.

Ben
